chunks: Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi from Hamedan, upon his return from Hajj, narrated to us; Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Dimashqi narrated to him; Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to him; Muslima ibn Ali narrated from al-A'mash, from al-Shaqiq, from al-Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

O assembly of Muslims, beware of adultery, for it contains six characteristics: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world, it removes beauty (al-baha'), causes poverty, and shortens life. As for those in the Hereafter, it incurs the Wrath of the Lord, results in a bad reckoning, and leads to eternal residence in the Fire.
Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) added: "It was made appealing to them by their own souls that the Wrath of Allah is upon them and in the Punishment they will abide eternally."
ai.seo_question: What are the six consequences of adultery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal*, this hadith from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman categorizes the six consequences of *zina* into worldly and otherworldly realms, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the holistic impact of sin on both physical well-being and spiritual destiny. The narration concludes by linking the sin to Quranic verse 14:22, illustrating how the self (*nafs*) deceives individuals into embracing Divine wrath, a theme central to moral psychology in Shia exegesis.
